The goal of the game is to collect cards in the <color=#FCA311>'Foundations'</color> at the top.
Drag the face-up <color=#8294FF>Six of Spades (6♠)</color> to the first <color=#FCA311>Foundation</color>.

On the <color=#FCA311>Tableau</color>, cards are stacked in descending order with alternating colors.
Drag the <color=#8294FF>black Ten of Clubs (10♣)</color> onto the <color=#FF6B6B>red Jack of Diamonds (J♦)</color>.

Great, a hidden card has been revealed! They can be quickly sent to the <color=#FCA311>Foundation</color> with a double click.
Double-click on the <color=#FF6B6B>Six of Hearts (6♥)</color>.

<color=#FCA311>ONLY</color> Kings can be placed in empty slots on the board.
Drag the <color=#FF6B6B>King of Hearts (K♥)</color> to the first empty column.

You can move multiple face-up cards at once.
Move the stack with the <color=#FF6B6B>red Ten of Diamonds (10♦)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>black Jack of Clubs (J♣)</color>.
No available moves? Use the <color=#FCA311>Stock</color> (top left). Click on it to draw a card.
We drew a <color=#8294FF>Ten of Spades (10♠)</color>. Place it on the revealed <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Hearts (J♥)</color>.
Great move! But sometimes an action needs to be undone. Let's check how the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button at the bottom of the screen works.
Return the <color=#8294FF>Ten of Spades (10♠)</color> back to the <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Hearts (J♥)</color>.

Sometimes it is beneficial to return a card from the <color=#FCA311>Foundation</color> back to the board.
Drag the <color=#FF6B6B>Nine of Diamonds (9♦)</color> from the <color=#FCA311>Foundation</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>black Ten of Spades (10♠)</color>.

There is one last card left in our tutorial <color=#FCA311>deck</color>. Let's draw it!
Click on the deck.
Place the <color=#FF6B6B>Nine of Hearts (9♥)</color> on the <color=#8294FF>Ten of Clubs (10♣)</color>.

The deck is empty! Now let's send the revealed cards to the <color=#FCA311>Foundation</color>.
Double-click on the <color=#8294FF>Seven of Spades (7♠)</color>.
All cards are revealed. Press the <color=#FCA311>'AUTO'</color> button!
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have mastered all the mechanics. Good luck in the game!

In Spider, cards are stacked in descending order.
Drag the <color=#8294FF>Eight of Spades (8♠)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>Nine of Spades (9♠)</color>.

Great, a hidden card has been revealed!
Stacks of the <color=#FCA311>same suit</color> can be moved as a whole. Move the <color=#8294FF>7♠-6♠-5♠</color> stack onto your Eight.

You can place cards on top of each other regardless of suit.
Place the <color=#FF6B6B>Four of Hearts (4♥)</color> onto the black <color=#8294FF>Five of Spades (5♠)</color>.

Attention: mixed-suit stacks are <color=#FF6B6B>blocked</color>! They cannot be moved together.
Press <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> to return the card.

To deal new cards from the deck, there must be no empty slots on the tableau!
Move the <color=#8294FF>King of Spades (K♠)</color> to the empty column on the right.
Now all slots are filled. Click on the <color=#FCA311>deck</color> in the bottom right corner to deal a new row of cards.

We got the Aces we needed! But the Twos are covered by new cards.
Move the <color=#8294FF>Three of Spades (3♠)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>Four of Spades (4♠)</color>.
The path is clear! Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Ace of Hearts (A♥)</color> onto the <color=#FF6B6B>Two of Hearts (2♥)</color> to complete the sequence!

Great! Now let's free the second Two.
Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Four of Hearts (4♥)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>Five of Spades (5♠)</color>.
And now move the <color=#8294FF>Ace of Spades (A♠)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>Two of Spades (2♠)</color> in the last remaining stack.
Congratulations! You have mastered all the mechanics of Spider!

The main feature of this solitaire is the 4 <color=#FCA311>Free Cells</color>.
The <color=#8294FF>Ace of Spades (A♠)</color> is blocked. Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Eight of Hearts (8♥)</color> to a <color=#FCA311>Free Cell</color> (top left).
The Ace is free! Press <color=#FCA311>'AUTO'</color> to send all available cards to the <color=#FCA311>Foundations</color>.

Just like in Klondike, cards on the tableau alternate in color.
Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Seven of Diamonds (7♦)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>Eight of Clubs (8♣)</color>.

The <color=#FCA311>indicator</color> next to the Auto button shows the max stack length you can move (currently 4).
Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Ten of Diamonds (10♦)</color> into a <color=#FCA311>Free Cell</color> to free up the column.

The indicator has changed (6/3). The second number is the limit for an <color=#FCA311>empty column</color>.
Move the stack (<color=#8294FF>6♠</color> and <color=#FF6B6B>5♥</color>) into the empty column.
Any move can be undone. Let's check how the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button at the bottom of the screen works.
Now move this stack (<color=#8294FF>6♠</color> and <color=#FF6B6B>5♥</color>) onto the <color=#FF6B6B>Seven of Diamonds (7♦)</color>.
Tutorial completed! Press <color=#FCA311>'AUTO'</color> to collect the remaining cards and win!
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have mastered all the rules of FreeCell. Good luck in the game!

In Pyramid, you need to remove cards in pairs that add up to <color=#FCA311>13</color>. A King equals 13 and can be removed with a single click.
Click on the <color=#8294FF>King of Spades (K♠)</color>.

Queen (12) + Ace (1) = <color=#FCA311>13</color>.
Click first on the <color=#FF6B6B>Queen of Diamonds (Q♦)</color> and then on the <color=#8294FF>Ace of Clubs (A♣)</color> to remove them.
Forgot a card's value? Press the <color=#FCA311>'Hint'</color> button at the top.
There are no matching pairs on the table. Click the <color=#FCA311>button</color> under the deck to reveal new cards. Note: only <color=#FCA311>2 redeals</color> are available!

Great! Five (5) + Eight (8) = <color=#FCA311>13</color>.
Match the <color=#8294FF>Five of Spades (5♠)</color> from the deck with the <color=#8294FF>Eight of Spades (8♠)</color> on the table.
Great move! But sometimes an action needs to be undone. Press the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button at the bottom of the screen.
Now let's match the <color=#8294FF>Five of Spades (5♠)</color> and the <color=#8294FF>Eight of Spades (8♠)</color> again.

Nine (9) + Four (4) = <color=#FCA311>13</color>.
Match the <color=#FF6B6B>Nine of Hearts (9♥)</color> in the deck with the <color=#8294FF>Four of Clubs (4♣)</color>.

The path is clear! There's a Seven at the peak and our Six in the waste.
Click on the <color=#FF6B6B>Six of Diamonds (6♦)</color> and the <color=#FF6B6B>Seven of Hearts (7♥)</color>!

The goal is to <color=#FCA311>remove all cards</color>. Choose face-up cards that are <color=#FCA311>1 rank higher or lower</color> than the card in the waste pile (currently it's <color=#8294FF>5♠</color>). Build long <color=#FCA311>combos</color> for points!
Remove: <color=#FF6B6B>6♥</color> -> <color=#8294FF>7♣</color> -> <color=#FF6B6B>8♦</color>.
There are no more available moves. Draw a new card from the <color=#FCA311>deck</color>.

We drew a <color=#FF6B6B>Queen (Q♦)</color>. Card ranks go <color=#FCA311>in a loop</color>: an <color=#FF6B6B>Ace (A)</color> can be played on a <color=#8294FF>King (K)</color>, and a <color=#8294FF>Two (2)</color> on an Ace. Complete this chain!
Let's check how the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button works. Click on it.
Great! Return the <color=#8294FF>Two of Clubs (2♣)</color> and clear the board: <color=#8294FF>2</color> -> <color=#FF6B6B>3</color> -> <color=#8294FF>4</color> -> <color=#FF6B6B>5</color>!

Our game has two variants: <color=#FCA311>'Classic'</color> and <color=#FCA311>'Russian'</color>. In Classic, cards alternate in color.
Move the <color=#8294FF>black Ten of Spades (10♠)</color> onto the <color=#FF6B6B>red Jack of Hearts (J♥)</color>.

The rules of the <color=#FCA311>'Russian'</color> variant are different — cards are stacked strictly by suit.
Let's move that same <color=#8294FF>Ten of Spades (10♠)</color> onto the <color=#8294FF>Jack of Spades (J♠)</color> to see how it works.

Great! Now we know both variants. Let's undo this move and continue the tutorial with classic rules.
Press the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button.

The main feature of Yukon is moving stacks. You can grab <color=#FCA311>ANY</color> face-up card and drag the entire massive stack on top of it!
Take the <color=#8294FF>black Queen of Clubs (Q♣)</color> from the last column and move it onto the <color=#FF6B6B>red King of Hearts (K♥)</color>.

Cards can be quickly sent to the <color=#FCA311>Foundations</color> with a double click.
Let's send the <color=#8294FF>Ten of Clubs (10♣)</color> there!

<color=#FCA311>ONLY</color> Kings can be placed in empty slots on the board.
Move the <color=#8294FF>King of Spades (K♠)</color> into the empty column to reveal the card underneath.

You have mastered all the mechanics! There are no more face-down cards on the board.
Press the <color=#FCA311>'AUTO'</color> button to quickly finish the game!
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have mastered all the mechanics of Yukon. Good luck in the game!

In Monte Carlo, you need to remove pairs of identical cards.
First is the <color=#FCA311>'8 Ways'</color> rule. Click on two adjacent Fives: <color=#FF6B6B>(5♥)</color> and <color=#8294FF>(5♠)</color>.

The cards have shifted! Now the <color=#FCA311>'4 Ways'</color> mode (cross-shaped) is active.
The Sevens ended up on top of each other. Remove <color=#FF6B6B>(7♦)</color> and <color=#8294FF>(7♣)</color>!

Back to the <color=#FCA311>'8 Ways'</color> mode! Now you can match diagonally as well.
Remove the two Kings: <color=#FF6B6B>(K♥)</color> and <color=#8294FF>(K♠)</color>.

Great move! But let's check how <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> works.
Press the Undo button at the bottom of the screen.

The Kings are back in place. You know all the rules!
Finish the game by removing all remaining pairs.
Keep removing pairs until total victory!
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have mastered the rules of Monte Carlo!

The goal of the game is to collect all cards in the <color=#FCA311>Foundations</color> around the Sultan (King of Hearts).
Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Hearts (J♥)</color> from the <color=#FCA311>Reserve</color> to the appropriate Foundation.

In 'Sultan', the deck can be flipped through <color=#FCA311>only 2 times</color> during the entire game!
Click on the <color=#FCA311>deck</color> to reveal a new card.

We drew a <color=#8294FF>Jack of Clubs (J♣)</color>. It is not needed right now, since the Clubs Foundations need Tens first.
Move it to an <color=#FCA311>empty Reserve slot</color>.

Great move! But empty spots in the reserve are very valuable, so it's better to save them.
Press the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button at the bottom of the screen.

Let's see what the next card is.
Click on the <color=#FCA311>deck</color> one more time.

It's a <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Diamonds (J♦)</color>! It fits perfectly.
Send it from the waste directly to the correct <color=#FCA311>Foundation</color>.

Cards can be quickly moved with a <color=#FCA311>double click</color>. The game will choose the spot itself: checking Foundations first, then the Reserve.
Double-click on the <color=#8294FF>Jack of Clubs (J♣)</color>.
Great! The Jack flew into the empty Reserve. Now let's draw another card from the <color=#FCA311>deck</color>.
It's a <color=#8294FF>Ten of Clubs (10♣)</color>, and the Foundations need it! Click on it <color=#FCA311>twice</color>, and it will fly straight to the base.

You have mastered all the rules of Sultan solitaire!
Finish the game on your own by distributing the <color=#FCA311>remaining cards</color>.
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have successfully mastered Sultan solitaire!

Welcome to Octagon! Victory is just around the corner. Let's reveal some new cards: click on the <color=#FCA311>deck</color>. Note: you can flip through the deck <color=#FCA311>only 2 times</color> per game!

On the table, cards are stacked in descending order, and the suit can be <color=#FCA311>ANY</color>.
Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Queen of Hearts (Q♥)</color> from the waste onto the <color=#8294FF>King of Clubs (K♣)</color> on the table.

Only one card is left in the left group of slots. Move the <color=#8294FF>Jack of Clubs (J♣)</color> onto our <color=#FF6B6B>Queen of Hearts (Q♥)</color>. The group will empty and <color=#FCA311>automatically fill up</color> with new cards!
The new cards didn't help us right now, and the Jack blocked the card we needed. Let's return everything back! Press the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button.

Sometimes, to save the situation, you can take a needed card directly from a Foundation! (You just can't take Aces and Kings). Pull the <color=#FF6B6B>Queen of Diamonds (Q♦)</color> from the Foundation and place it on the <color=#8294FF>King of Spades (K♠)</color>.

Brilliant! A double click sends a card to a Foundation, OR to the table, but on the table <color=#FCA311>the suit must match exactly</color>. Double-click on the <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Diamonds (J♦)</color>.
By removing the Jack, we unlocked the final cards! Now double-click on the revealed <color=#FF6B6B>King of Hearts (K♥)</color>, and it will go straight to the Foundation.

You have mastered all the mechanics of Octagon!
There are only a few face-up cards left on the table. Distribute them among the <color=#FCA311>Foundations</color> and finish the game!
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have successfully completed the tutorial and solved Octagon solitaire!

The goal of 'Montana' is to arrange the cards by suit from Ace to King in 4 rows. Only Aces can be placed in empty slots on the LEFT. Drag the <color=#8294FF>Ace of Spades (A♠)</color> into the first empty slot.
Great move! But sometimes an action needs to be undone. Let's check how the <color=#FCA311>'Undo'</color> button at the bottom of the screen works. Click on it.
The Ace is back! Cards can be quickly sent to their place with a double click. Double-click on the <color=#8294FF>Ace of Spades (A♠)</color>.
A Two of the same suit must follow an Ace. Double-click on the <color=#8294FF>Two of Spades (2♠)</color>.
Continue the row! Send the <color=#8294FF>Three of Spades (3♠)</color> to the Two with a double click.
Great! Keep moving Spades as long as there are available moves!
Now send the remaining Aces into the empty slots on the left with a double click! Start with the <color=#8294FF>Ace of Clubs (A♣)</color>.
You've hit a dead end! All empty slots ended up strictly behind Kings, and you cannot place cards after Kings. Press <color=#FCA311>'Redeal'</color>!

The <color=#FCA311>'Hard'</color> mode is currently active: empty slots after a redeal ONLY appear at the end of a row. Move the <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Hearts (J♥)</color> into the empty slot behind the Ten.
A slot behind the Seven of Spades has opened up! Now confidently send the <color=#8294FF>Eight of Spades (8♠)</color> there with a double click.

Another dead end! Press <color=#FCA311>'Redeal'</color> once more. We are returning to the <color=#FCA311>'Classic'</color> mode — empty slots will conveniently appear right behind the assembled cards!
Almost done! The cards miraculously came together, just the final push remains. Send the <color=#FF6B6B>Jack of Hearts (J♥)</color> to its place.
And finally, the <color=#FF6B6B>King of Hearts (K♥)</color> for an absolute victory!
<color=#FCA311>Congratulations!</color> You have masterfully learned the rules of Montana!
